transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-05
Start: 16:00 UTC
Scheduled duration: 60 minutes (ran ~62)
Attendees: Alex Kim, Priya Shah - Redwood; Jorge Alvarez (CISO), Maya Singh (Platform), Evan Brooks (Compliance) - LumenBank

Summary (auto): quick deep dive on audit exports and admin activity; agreement to run export PoC and share schema docs.

00:00 Alex Kim: okay, thanks everyone for joining, um, I think we have about an hour, we'll try to focus on the audit exports and admin activity events, so we're clear on what you need and what we can deliver.
00:18 Jorge Alvarez: thanks Alex, yeah this is Jorge, real quick context from our side: we're migrating a lot of user-facing flows to a new platform and compliance is asking for immutable admin trails and exportability to our SIEM and long-term cold storage.
00:36 Priya Shah: great, can you share the systems that need to ingest the logs? is it Splunk, or Kafka, or both?
00:45 Maya Singh: primarily Splunk and a Kafka topic for internal analytics. Also we have a retention engine that pulls S3 buckets.
00:53 Alex Kim: cool, thanks. quick orientation: Redwood emits two high-level categories — "admin events" which are changes to configuration, role grants, model rollouts, and "audit logs" which are request-level events, token usage, and system actions. We can export both.
01:10 Evan Brooks: when you say request-level, do you include user identity mapping? like when a user triggers a model invocation under an impersonation or service account?
01:20 Priya Shah: yes, we include the authenticated principal field, but there are caveats around proxied requests and SSO mapping — sometimes the SAML nameid is present, sometimes a local session id is used. we can surface the mapping table.
01:34 Jorge Alvarez: that's important — we need to prove who did what for audits. we also need to know retention and immutable export guarantees.
01:44 Alex Kim: understood. brief on exports: we support S3 exports (batched hourly/daily), streaming to Kafka (producer to your topic), and syslog/HTTPS webhooks for real-time streaming. S3 exports can be configured with server-side encryption using SSE-KMS and with object locks for WORM-like retention.
02:05 Maya Singh: object lock — that would satisfy our legal hold workflows?
02:09 Priya Shah: for S3 we can enable object lock when you use our managed export process, but note we don't manage your bucket policy — we deliver objects into a bucket you control, so the lock and governance is on your side. we do support delivering to a Redwood-owned bucket on enterprise contracts if required.
02:28 Evan Brooks: can you clarify what fields are in the admin event? does it capture the before/after state of the change?
02:35 Alex Kim: yes, admin events include a change delta block where available — e.g., role change: before: {"roles": [...]}, after: {...}. sometimes the delta is redacted for sensitive fields (we'll mark in schema).
02:50 Maya Singh: redacted how? is it consistent? sometimes we need non-redacted for internal forensics.
02:56 Priya Shah: redaction is policy-driven; by default we redact secrets and API keys. for forensics you can request full deltas under a compliance contract and we can stream those when agreed, with stricter KMS/HSM usage and customer-managed keys.
03:12 Jorge Alvarez: okay, so a few requirements from compliance: immutable auditable export with customer-managed KMS keys, retention >= 7 years for admin trails, and ability to feed to our SIEM with minimum 1 minute latency. feasible?
03:28 Alex Kim: generally yes. details: S3 export with SSE-KMS using your CMK — we support key policies and grants; Kafka can be TLS + client auth. For sub-minute delivery, Kafka/syslog is the path; S3 is typically batch (we do hourly small-file rollups but can do more frequent if needed).
03:46 Evan Brooks: about KMS/HSM — do you allow use of our external HSM for envelope encryption?
03:52 Priya Shah: we currently integrate with cloud KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) for customer-managed keys. For direct HSM integration (on-prem HSM) we offer an enterprise option where keys are stored in a customer side HSM and Redwood encrypts with a wrapping key. that requires an enterprise contract and additional attestation.
04:12 Mariana (mis-transcribed as Mariah) — note: speaker labels in export might be off sometimes
04:16 Maya Singh: another question — what about event fidelity when RBAC changes are done via API vs UI? we saw earlier that some systems only log event id without full context.
04:29 Priya Shah: good question. both API and UI actions hit the same audit pipeline. but metadata may differ — UI actions include session context (browser user agent, IP), API calls include token fingerprint, origin service. we'll show examples in the schema.
04:45 Alex Kim: quick demo link I'll share after call — a sample S3 payload and a live Kafka consumer showing admin events.
04:52 Jorge Alvarez: about data residency — can we ensure audit exports stay in eu-west-1? we can't ship logs outside region.
04:58 Priya Shah: yes, region pinning for storage is supported. Redwood will deliver exports to the region-specific bucket you provision; for streaming the Kafka endpoint can be in-region. note that if you use Redwood-managed backups that cross regions, we can disable that.
05:18 Evan Brooks: what about retention enforcement and deletions — if a user requests deletion for GDPR, do those admin logs need to be deleted? that conflicts with retention.
05:28 Alex Kim: common tension. we support dual policies: operational logs vs compliance trails. compliance trails (admin events) can be configured as immutable with legal hold to prevent deletion; personal data in request logs can be redacted at ingestion if you need erasure. we should map your GDPR needs in the PoC.
05:46 Maya Singh: ok, please show the schema.
05:50 Alex Kim: yep. I'll paste schema in chat after. example fields: timestamp, tenant_id, principal_id, principal_type, action, resource_type, resource_id, change_delta, request_id, correlation_id, ip, user_agent, auth_method, saml_nameid, role_changes, outcome (success/fail), error_code, retention_class.
06:12 Jorge Alvarez: retention_class?
06:14 Priya Shah: that's internal tag we emit to mark e.g., "compliance" vs "operational". You can map ingestion policies on your side.
06:22 Evan Brooks: is there an event id we can rely on for deduping across retries?
06:26 Alex Kim: yes, request_id is stable and we add a monotonic event_sequence per tenant for ordering in exports. in Kafka we keep those as message keys.
06:38 Maya Singh: latency expectations for Kafka?
06:41 Priya Shah: typical 100-300ms to our broker, then depends on network — we recommend provisioned throughput and a small producer ack policy for sub-second guarantees.
06:52 Jorge Alvarez: SOC2 evidence: can you provide logs of admin activity for audits, like a historical pull?
06:58 Alex Kim: yes, for SOC2 audits we can provide evidence exports; Redwood keeps internal audit history and can provide exports for a period aligned with the contract. the SOC 2 report itself and controls matrix will be attached.
07:12 Evan Brooks: is there a way to trigger an on-demand export for a specific time range?
07:16 Priya Shah: yes — on-demand exports via the console or API; we create a signed manifest and push to your S3 or deliver to a temp Kafka topic.
07:25 Jorge Alvarez: any caveats around PII — do request payloads include user-provided content? we need to avoid that in logs.
07:33 Alex Kim: request payloads are not included in the standard operational audit log; we do include metadata about the request and tokens used but not the prompt content unless you explicitly enable full request logging (again, contract-only for sensitive data).
07:52 Maya Singh: we need to see examples for our security team — particularly how role grants and admin API keys are represented.
07:58 Priya Shah: noted. we'll include examples for role grant events showing before/after, actor metadata, and whether MFA or SSO used.
08:08 Jorge Alvarez: how does SSO mapping affect user identifiers? we use Okta with nameID format transient vs persistent.
08:15 Alex Kim: we ingest SAML attributes as provided; if nameID is transient we recommend mapping SAML to your internal unique id and storing mapping table. Redwood can store the mapping if you want; we can also emit both the external identity and our internal user_id.
08:29 Evan Brooks: for forensic purposes we need IP and session start/stop correlated — do you log session lifecycle events?
08:36 Priya Shah: yes, session start/stop with session ids are captured. we also emit heartbeat pings for long running sessions.
08:44 Maya Singh: retention costs — can you give a rough unit cost for keeping admin events for 7 years in cold storage?
08:50 Alex Kim: we don't bill storage for S3 exports — you pay AWS. Redwood can include an add-on for long-term archival management with retrieval SLAs; we'll put approximate pricing in the follow-up.
09:00 Jorge Alvarez: legal hold automation — if a case is opened we need to lock certain tenant data.
09:06 Priya Shah: we support tagging of tenant exports with legal hold flag; we can also store legal-hold manifests that prevent Redwood from rotating or deleting exports. enforcement on your S3 side is recommended for end-to-end immutability.
09:20 Alex Kim: quick note — some customers use a hybrid: Kafka for realtime alerting to SIEM + S3 for immutable long term. That seems to be your plan?
09:29 Maya Singh: yes. prefer Kafka for alerts and S3 for archive.
09:33 Evan Brooks: encryption in transit? TLS only or mutual TLS?
09:36 Priya Shah: TLS 1.2+ with option for mTLS for Kafka. Syslog over TLS is supported.
09:42 Jorge Alvarez: about audit log schema changes — how are schema migrations handled when you change event shape?
09:47 Alex Kim: we version schemas and include a schema_version field in every message. We keep prior versions available for a year and provide migration notes. If you rely on strict schema, we can provide a compatibility mode.
09:59 Maya Singh: do you support Avro/Confluent registry?
10:03 Priya Shah: yes, Kafka exports can be Avro with schema registry or JSON. We'll support whatever your consumer expects.
10:10 Evan Brooks: need to confirm retention start dates — is it event ingestion time or export time?
10:15 Alex Kim: retention_class timestamps are ingestion time; exports show both ingestion_time and export_time. for legal hold you can lock based on ingestion_time.
10:24 Jorge Alvarez: one more on integrity — do you sign the exported objects so we can verify tamper?
10:30 Priya Shah: yes, we can provide an HMAC signature header and optionally PGP sign the manifest for non-repudiation. If you need full chain-of-custody, we can generate attestations.
10:44 Maya Singh: great. show us the webhook option — our SIEM can accept HTTPS posts. do you retry on failure?
10:50 Alex Kim: webhook endpoint supports retries with exponential backoff and dead-letter to S3 after X attempts. You can also configure ack requirements.
10:58 Jorge Alvarez: curious about auditability of RBAC changes that come from automated systems — are API keys used by infra bots captured as principal type bot?
11:06 Priya Shah: we tag auth_method and principal_type (human, service, bot). token metadata includes token_owner when available so you can trace to the CI job.
11:18 Evan Brooks: what about change tracking for configuration drifts — do you capture who changed autoscaling policies,etc?
11:22 Alex Kim: yes, configuration changes across infra and model rollout - all captured as admin events with delta.
11:28 Maya Singh: ok next: schema and example exports.
11:31 Alex Kim: I'll drop links. [link placeholder: https://redwood.ai/docs/audit-exports/sample-schema.json] (note: auto-transcription may mangle link)
11:45 Priya Shah: demo note: we will prepare a small S3 export with SSE-KMS using your CMK and a Kafka demo topic with Avro to show both paths.
11:53 Jorge Alvarez: for the PoC we want sample events for: role grant/revoke, model rollback, workspace deletion, policy change, token creation.
12:02 Alex Kim: noted. we'll include those event types.
12:05 Evan Brooks: about retention classification, can you tag records and we can set lifecycle policies?
12:10 Priya Shah: yes. retention_class and retention_expires_at fields included.
12:14 Jorge Alvarez: compliance wants a test where we retrieve and verify signed manifests for a 3-week-old export. can we do that?
12:21 Alex Kim: yes, we'll include manifest signing in the PoC.
12:25 Maya Singh: are there limits on the volume of export events? we anticipate spikes during incidents.
12:32 Priya Shah: we support burst buffers, but for Kafka you should provision partitions; for S3 we shard files by timestamp and tenant to handle spikes. for extremely large bursts we have backpressure options.
12:46 Evan Brooks: any throttling on historical pulls?
12:49 Alex Kim: historical exports are gated by rate limits — we'll coordinate bulk extracts with a scheduled window as part of the PoC.
12:58 Jorge Alvarez: last one, for audit trails we need immutable chronological ordering. how do you handle clock skew?
13:05 Priya Shah: we include both device_time and ingest_time and use monotonic event_sequence for ordering; we also provide clock skew metrics per host forensics.
13:16 Alex Kim: ok, recap and next steps — we'll share schema and sample payloads by Tuesday, schedule the PoC workshop, and Priya will run the demo export.
13:28 Jorge Alvarez: thanks all. we'll confirm workshop attendees and the Kafka sysadmin.
13:33 Evan Brooks: thanks, appreciate it.
13:36 Alex Kim: thanks everyone — I'll send the follow up with the links and action items.

Post-call notes (auto): audio had a bit of overlap 11:30-11:45. There were a few mis-transcribed names (Mariana/Mariah). Redwood to supply docs: schema, SOC2 summary, KMS architecture and pricing add-on. Customer will prepare list of SIEM endpoints, Kafka config, and retention policy.
